questions.q: Width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit interference experiment is half of the other slit. The ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{I} \propto$ width $\quad \mathrm{I}_{\max }=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2}\right)^2$
$\therefore \mathrm{I}_1=\mathrm{I}_0, \mathrm{I}_2=2 \mathrm{I}_0 \quad \mathrm{I}_{\min }=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2}\right)^2$
$\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)^2}{(\sqrt{2}-1)^2} \Rightarrow \frac{3+2 \sqrt{2}}{3-2 \sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: An unpolarised light beam of intensity $2{I}_{0}$ is passed through a polaroid $P$ and then through another polaroid $Q$ which is oriented in such a way that its passing axis makes an angle of $30 °$ relative to that of $P$. The intensity of the emergent light is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When unpolarized light passes from Polaroid, then it becomes polarised light and intensity becomes half of the original, therefore,& ${I}_{1} = \dfrac{2{I}_{0}}{2} = {I}_{0}$.

Given here,~$\theta = 30 °$.

Using law of~Malus~for the second polariser,~$I = {I}_{0}\cos^{2}\theta$

We have, intensity of emergent light,~${I}_{2} = {I}_{1}\cos^{2}30 °$

$= {I}_{0}\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{3{I}_{0}}{4}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : If the Brewster's angle for the light propagating from air to glass is ${θ}_{B}$, then Brewster's angle for the light propagating from glass to air is $\dfrac{π}{2} - {θ}_{B}$.

Statement II : The Brewster's angle for the light propagating from glass to air is $\tan^{- 1} \left({μ}_{g}\right), where ${μ}_{g}$ is the refractive index of glass.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

$
options: Both Statements I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Snell's law, we get

${μ}_{a}sini = {μ}_{g}sin \left(90 ° - i\right)$

$tani = $\dfrac{\mug}{\mua}

When going from glass to air
$tani^{'} = $\dfrac{\mua}{\mug} =$coti$

Clearly,~$i^{'} = \left(\dfrac{π}{2} -i\right)$& & hence& Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.q: A microwave of wavelength $2 . 0cm$ falls normally on a slit of width $4 . 0cm .$ The angular spread of the central maxima of the diffraction pattern obtained on a screen $1 . 5m$ away from the slit, will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Condition for minima is $\mathrm{d} \sin \theta=\mathrm{n} \lambda$
For Ist minimad $\sin \theta=\lambda\sin \theta=\frac{\lambda}{a}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2} \quad \therefore \theta=30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$
Angular spread $=2 \theta=60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$

questions.q: In Young's double slit arrangement, slits are separated by a gap of $0 . 5mm$, and the screen is placed at a distance of $0 . 5m$ from them. The distance between the first and the third bright fringe formed when the slits are illuminated by a monochromatic light of $5890\overset{o}{A}$& is :-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d} = \dfrac{5890 \times {10}^{- 10} \times 0 . 5}{0 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}}$
$= 589 \times {10}^{- 6}m$
Distance between first and third bright fringe is $2\beta = 2 \times 589 \times {10}^{- 6}m$
$= 1178 \times {10}^{- 6}m$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, three polarizers are kept as shown in the figure. The transmission axes of $P_1$ and $P_2$ are orthogonal to each other. The polarizer $P_3$ covers both the slits with its transmission axis at $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ to those of $P_1$ and $P_2$. An unpolarized light of wavelength $\lambda$ and intensity $I_0$ is incident on $P_1$ and $P_2$. The intensity at a point after $P_3$ where the path difference between the light waves from $s_1$ and $s_2$ is $\frac{\lambda}{3}$, is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: after passing through third poleriser, Intensity of both the waves must be $\frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4}$ now, at a point where path diff is $\frac{\lambda}{3}$, phase difference $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \phi=2 \mathrm{~K}\left(\frac{\Delta \mathrm{x}}{\lambda}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{res}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4}\right)^2+2\left(\frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4}\right)^2} \cos \frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{I}_0}{4} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: In young's double slit experiment, the fringe width is $12$ mm. If the entire arrangement is placed in water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$, then the fringe width becomes (in $mm$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a given light wavelength corresponding a medium of refractive index $\mu$

${λ}_{med} = \dfrac{\lambdavacumm}{μ}$.

And we know that fringe width $\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$

Therefore, ${β}_{med} = \dfrac{\betavacuum}{μ} = \dfrac{12}{43} = 9mm$

questions.q: Two polarisers $P_1$ and $P_2$ are placed in such a way that the intensity of the transmitted light will be zero. A third polariser $P_3$ is inserted in between $P_1$ and $\mathrm{P}_2$, at the particular angle between $\mathrm{P}_2$ and $\mathrm{P}_3$. The transmitted intensity of the light passing the through all three polarisers is maximum. The angle between the polarisers $\mathrm{P}_2$ and $\mathrm{P}_3$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Through $P_2 I_1=I_0 \sin ^2 $\$left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)

$I_1=I_0 \cos ^2 \theta$
Through $P_3 I_{\text {net }}=\left(I_0 \cos ^2 \theta\right) \sin ^2 \theta$
$I_{n c $t}=\frac{I_0}{4}[\sin (2 \theta)]^2 \text { for max } I_{\text {net }} \theta=45^{\circ}$
So angle between $P_2$ and P_3=\frac{\pi}{4}
Correct Ans. (1)$

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, light from two identical sources are superimposing on a screen. The path difference between the two lights reaching at a point on the screen is $\dfrac{7\lambda}{4}$. The ratio of intensity of fringe at this point with respect to the maximum intensity of the fringe is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the path difference is $∆ x = \dfrac{7\lambda}{4}$

Hence, the phase difference can be found as follows:

$\begin{cases}ϕ & = & \dfrac{2\pi}{λ} ∆ x \\ & = & \dfrac{2\pi}{λ} \times \dfrac{7\lambda}{4} \\ & = & \dfrac{7\pi}{2}\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the intensity is given by

$I = {I}_\max\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{ϕ}{2}\right) . . .\left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{I}{Imax}& = & $\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{ϕ}{2}\right)\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{2 \times 2}\right)$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\cos^{2} \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\cos^{2}\lleft(2\pi - \dfrac{π}{4}\right)\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \cos^{2}\dfrac{π}{4}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2}\end{cases}

$

questions.q: The width of fringe is $2$ mm on the screen in a double slit experiment for the light of wavelength of $400$ nm. The width of the fringe for the light of wavelength $600$ nm will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a light of wavelength& $\lambda$, the fringe width in~double slit experiment is given by

$\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d} . . . ( 1 )$

For a light of wavelength~$\lambda '$, the fringe width is given by

$\beta ' = \dfrac{\lambda ' D}{d} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the fringe width for the later case.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{\beta '}{β}$& = & $\dfrac{\lambda ' Dd}{\lambdaDd}$\\ & = & $\dfrac{\lambda '}{λ}$\\ & ⇒ & $\beta$' = $\dfrac{\lambda '}{\lambda}\beta . . . \left($3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required fringe width.

\begin{cases}\beta$' & = & $\dfrac{600nm}{400nm} \times$2mm \\ & = & 3mm\end{cases}

$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment slit separation $0.1mm,$ one observes a bright fringe at angle $\dfrac{1}{40}rad$ by using light of wavelength ${\lambda}_{1} .$ When the light of wavelength ${\lambda}_{2}$ is used a bright fringe is seen at the same angle in the same set up. Given that ${\lambda}_{1}$ and ${\lambda}_{2}$ are in visible range \left(380nmto740nm\right),$ their values are:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$dsin\theta = n\lambda$

$∴ \lambda = \dfrac{dsin\theta}{n} = {10}^{- 4} \times \dfrac{1}{40} \times \dfrac{1}{n}$

$∴ \lambda = \dfrac{2.5 \times {10}^{- 6}}{n} = \dfrac{2500 \times {10}^{- 9}}{n} = \dfrac{2500}{n} \left(nm\right)$

Putting $n = 1, {\lambda}_{1} = 2500nm$

$n = 2, {\lambda}_{2} = 1250nm$

$n = 3, {\lambda}_{3} = 833nm$

$n = 4, {\lambda}_{4} = 625nm$

$n = 5, {\lambda}_{5} = 500nm$

$n = 6, {\lambda}_{6} = 357nm$

questions.q: In young's double slit experiment performed using a monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, when a glass plate  \left(\mu = 1 . 5\right)$ of thickness $x\lambda$ is introduced in the path of the one of the interfering beams, the intensity at the position where the central maximum occurred previously remains unchanged. The value of $x$ will be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since& the intensity at the central maxima remains unchanged, the change in the path difference& should be an integral multiple of the wavelength. Therefore,

$\Deltax = \left(\mu - 1\right)t = n\lambda⇒ \left(1 . 5 - 1\right)x\lambda = n\lambda⇒ x = \dfrac{n}{0 . 5} = 2n$

For~$n = 1$

$x = 2$

questions.q:
In a Young’s double slit experiment, two slits are illuminated with a light of wavelength $800$ nm. The line joining ${A}_{1}P$ is perpendicular to ${A}_{1}{A}_{2}$ as shown in the figure. If the first minimum is detected at $P$, the value of slits separation~$a$~will be :

The distance of screen from slits $D = 5cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The position of first minima is

$y = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{2 \times a}$($y$~is height of the point from the axis passing through the mid-point of~${A}_{1}\text{and}{A}_{2}$)

Since the first minima is in front of the slit as shown in the figure,

$\dfrac{\lambdaD}{2 \times a} = \dfrac{a}{2}$

$⇒ a = \sqrt{\lambdaD} = \sqrt{800 \times {10}^{- 9} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 2 \times {10}^{- 4}m = 0 . 2mm$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, the path difference, at a certain point on the screen, betwen two interfering waves is $\frac{1}{8}$ th of wavelength. The ratio of the intensity at this point to that at the centre of a bright fringe is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, path difference, $\Delta x=\frac{\lambda}{8}$ Phase difference $(\Delta \phi)$ is given by $\Delta \phi=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}(\Delta \mathrm{x})\Delta \phi=\frac{(2 \pi)}{\lambda} \frac{\lambda}{8}=\frac{\pi}{4}$ For two sources in different phases,
I=I_{0} \cos ^{2} \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)$
$\frac{1}{I_{0}}=\cos ^{2} \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)$
$=\frac{1+\cos \frac{\pi}{4}}{2}=\frac{1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{2}=$0.85
$

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, an angular width of the fringe is $0 . 35 °$ on a screen placed at $2m$ away for particular wavelength of $450$ nm. The angular width of the fringe, when whole system is immersed in a medium of refractive index $\dfrac{7}{5}$, is $\dfrac{1}{α}$. The value of $\alpha$& is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular fringe width is given by& $\theta = \dfrac{λ}{D}$, where, $D$ is the distance between the source and the screen and~$\lambda$ is the wavelength of the light.

We have,~$\dfrac{\theta1}{\theta2} = \dfrac{\lambda1}{\lambda2}$

Then,~${θ}_{2} = \dfrac{0.35 ∘}{450nm} \times \dfrac{450nm}{\dfrac{7}{5}} = {0.25}^{∘} = \dfrac{1}{4}$~ ~ \left(∵ {λ}_{2} = \dfrac{\lambda1}{μ}\right)$

Thus, value of~$\alpha = 4$.

$

questions.q:
Unpolarised light is incident on the boundary between two dielectric media, whose dielectric constants are $2 . 8$ (medium −$1$) and $6 . 8$ (medium − $2$), respectively. To satisfy the condition, so that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other, the angle of incidence should be~$\tan^{- 1}\left(1 + \dfrac{10}{θ}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$,~the value of~$\theta$~is ______.

(Given for dielectric media, ${μ}_{r} = 1$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As given in the question, we can write

${μ}_{1} = \sqrt{{ε}_{r}{μ}_{r}} = \sqrt{2 . 8 \times 1} = \sqrt{2 . 8}$~and

${μ}_{2} = \sqrt{{ε}_{r}{μ}_{r}} = \sqrt{6 . 8 \times 1} = \sqrt{6 . 8}$

Now applying Snell's law and considering~$r = 90 ° - i$, we get

${μ}_{1}sini = {μ}_{2}cosi$

$⇒ tani = \dfrac{\mu2}{\mu1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6 . 8}{2 . 8}}$

$⇒ tani = \left(\dfrac{2 . 8 + 4}{2 . 8}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ i = \tan^{- 1}\left(1 + \dfrac{10}{7}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore,~$\theta = 7$.

questions.q: If the measured angular separation between the second minimum to the left of the central maximum and the third minimum to the right of the central maximum is $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ in a single slit diffraction pattern recorded using 628 nm light, then the width of the slit is _______ $\mu \mathrm{m}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \theta_1=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 \lambda}{a}\right) \\ & \theta_2=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3 \lambda}{a}\right) \\ & \because \quad \theta_1+\theta_2=30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 \lambda}{\mathrm{a}}\right)+\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3 \lambda}{\mathrm{a}}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{2 \lambda}{\mathrm{a}} \sqrt{1-\left(\frac{3 \lambda}{\mathrm{a}}\right)^2}+\frac{3 \lambda}{\mathrm{a}} \sqrt{1+\left(\frac{2 \lambda}{\mathrm{a}}\right)^2}=\sin \frac{\pi}{6}\end{aligned}$
Here $\lambda=628 \mathrm{~nm}$
After solving
$\mathrm{A}=6.07 \mu \mathrm{~m}$
Approximate Method :
$\begin{aligned} & \theta=\theta_1+\theta_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{2 \lambda}{a}+\frac{3 \lambda}{a} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{5}{a}(628 \mathrm{~nm}) \\ & \Rightarrow a=6 \mu \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$
